title: Can Big Food Adapt to Healthier Diets?

sentences: Big food, it seems, has a sweet tooth.
On August 14th Mars, a packaged-food giant best known for its chocolatey fare, announced it would gobble up Kellanova, maker of Pringles and Pop-Tarts, for $36bn.
It is not the only company betting big on calorific goodies.
Last November Smucker's, a purveyor of jams and peanut butters, completed its $6bn acquisition of Hostess Brands, maker of Ho Hos and Twinkies.
translations: 大型食品公司似乎偏爱甜食。
8月14日，以巧克力食品闻名的包装食品巨头玛氏宣布，将以360亿美元收购品客和Pop-Tarts的制造商Kellanova。
这并非唯一一家在高热量食品上押下重注的公司。
去年11月，果酱和花生酱供应商Smucker's完成了对Ho Hos和Twinkies制造商Hostess Brands的60亿美元收购。

sentences: Filling bellies is a lucrative business.
The West's ten most valuable packaged-food and soft-drink companies have a combined market capitalisation of around $1trn.
Their average operating margin last year was a plump 17%; grocers typically make just 2-4%.
Consumers have continued to feast on the cheap calories served up by these firms despite the recent bout of inflation.
translations: 填饱肚子是一门利润丰厚的生意。
西方十大最有价值的包装食品和软饮料公司的总市值约为1万亿美元。
它们去年的平均营业利润率高达17%；而杂货商通常只有2-4%。
尽管近期通胀高企，消费者仍继续大快朵颐这些公司提供的廉价热量。

sentences: Yet the industry also faces threats.
The impact of its products on the health of those who consume them has long been a concern for shoppers and policymakers alike.
Consumers may now indulge on them less as weight-loss drugs become cheaper and more convenient.
translations: 然而，该行业也面临着威胁。
其产品对消费者健康的影响长期以来一直是购物者和政策制定者共同关注的问题。
随着减肥药物变得更便宜、更方便，消费者现在可能较少沉迷于这些产品。

sentences: What is more, a growing body of research suggests that it may not only be an excess of sugar, fat and salt that causes health problems, but also the heavy processing used to whip up cheap nibbles.
Both are set to reshape the industry — and transform what the world ingests.
translations: 此外，越来越多的研究表明，导致健康问题的可能不仅仅是过量的糖、脂肪和盐，还有用于制作廉价零食的深度加工过程。
这两者都将重塑食品行业，并改变全世界的饮食内容。

sentences: The roots of today's food industry stretch back to 19th-century innovations such as pasteurisation and canning that helped make food plentiful, convenient and safe.

Today a humble bag of crisps is manufactured in an assembly line where spuds are sliced, fried, drenched in seasoning, preservatives, and colouring agents, then sealed in a bag with nitrogen to keep them from going stale.
The process takes around 30 minutes.
translations: 当今食品工业的根源可追溯至19世纪的创新，如巴氏杀菌和罐装技术，这些技术帮助使食品变得丰富、便捷且安全。
如今，一袋普通的薯片在流水线上生产：土豆被切片、油炸，浸入调味料、防腐剂和着色剂，然后用氮气密封在袋中以防变质。
整个过程大约需要30分钟。

sentences: Such tasty products have contributed to the surge in obesity in recent decades.

According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation, the average daily calorie intake of people in the rich world has risen by a fifth since the 1960s, to 3,500 calories, well in excess of what their bodies need.
By the end of this decade nearly half the world's population is expected to be obese or overweight.
translations: 这些美味的食品是近几十年来肥胖率激增的原因之一。
根据联合国粮农组织的数据，自20世纪60年代以来，富裕国家居民的人均每日卡路里摄入量增加了五分之一，达到3500卡路里，远超身体所需。
到本十年末，预计全球近一半的人口将面临肥胖或超重问题。

sentences: Consumers who have found it difficult to alter their diets may at last be able to do so thanks to new blockbuster weight-loss drugs.
translations: 那些发现难以改变饮食习惯的消费者，最终可能因新型重磅减肥药物而得以实现这一目标。

sentences: Patients taking the drugs have reported that they crave calorific food less.
Analysis by Grocery Doppio, a research firm, finds that users lower their spending on groceries by 11% on average, with spending on snacks and confectionery falling by more than half.
Morgan Stanley, a bank, reckons 7-9% of Americans could be taking weight-loss drugs by 2035, resulting in reductions in overall demand ranging from 3% for cereal to 5% for ice cream.
translations: 服用这些药物的患者报告称，他们对高热量食物的渴望减少了。
研究公司Grocery Doppio的分析发现，用户平均在食品杂货上的支出减少了11%，其中零食和糖果的支出下降了一半以上。
摩根士丹利银行估计，到2035年，7%至9%的美国人可能会服用减肥药，导致整体需求减少，从谷物的3%到冰淇淋的5%不等。

sentences: Big food may well take these developments in its stride.
The industry has a record of launching new products that cater to weight-watching consumers.
Coca-Cola first launched Diet Coke in 1982, and has released various other sugar-free alternatives since then.
translations: 大型食品公司很可能会从容应对这些发展。
该行业有推出迎合体重管理消费者的新产品的记录。
可口可乐于1982年首次推出健怡可乐，此后又发布了多种其他无糖替代品。

sentences: Most food and beverage companies now offer products with reduced sugar, fat or salt.
According to Mintel, a market-research firm, the number of new health-conscious snacks launched annually rose by 2% between 2015 and 2020, compared with a decline of 1% for traditional snacks.
Some companies, such as Mondelez, an American snack giant, now offer smaller portion sizes.
translations: 大多数食品和饮料公司现在都提供减糖、减脂或减盐的产品。
根据市场研究公司Mintel的数据，2015年至2020年间，每年推出的注重健康的新零食数量增长了2%，而传统零食则下降了1%。
一些公司，例如美国零食巨头亿滋，现在提供更小份量的产品。

sentences: The threat from a crackdown on processed foods, if it materialises, will be trickier to deal with.
In 2009 Carlos Monteiro, a Brazilian scientist, sorted food into four buckets based on the degree of processing undertaken.
translations: 如果对加工食品的打击成为现实，这一威胁将更难应对。
2009年，巴西科学家卡洛斯·蒙泰罗根据加工程度将食品分为四类。

sentences: The first covers unprocessed items such as fruit and vegetables.

The last, called ultra-processed foods (UPFs), covers items such as breakfast cereal and crisps, as well as protein bars and fake meats, which contain significant amounts of ingredients not typically found in a home kitchen.
Since the 1990s the share of UPFs in diets worldwide has been increasing.
translations: 第一类涵盖未加工食品，如水果和蔬菜。
最后一类被称为超加工食品（UPFs），包括早餐麦片、薯片、蛋白棒和仿制肉等，这些食品含有大量家庭厨房中通常不常见的成分。
自20世纪90年代以来，超加工食品在全球饮食中的占比一直在上升。

sentences: Ditching additives could make products more expensive to produce and shorten their shelf life, cutting into profits.
Big food has so far managed to thrive even as concerns around consumers' health have swirled.
With upfs, it could face its most daunting challenge yet.
translations: 放弃添加剂可能会使产品生产成本更高，缩短保质期，从而削减利润。
尽管围绕消费者健康的担忧不断涌现，大型食品公司迄今仍设法蓬勃发展。
面对超加工食品，它可能面临迄今为止最严峻的挑战。
